lead_story.headline: Upstream Monopoly Foreclosure: FTC Shifts Antitrust Crosshairs from LLM Weights to Power & Substation Capacity
lead_story.image_caption: High-voltage 500kV utility interconnection substation and generator busbar switchyard.
lead_story.image_alt: High-voltage electrical substation and generator busbar switchyard
lead_story.catch_up: In a decisive doctrine shift, FTC leadership confirmed that federal antitrust scrutiny is pivoting upstream. Rather than policing downstream foundation model releases, regulators are targeting exclusive hyperscaler power purchase agreements (PPAs), captive Behind-the-Meter (BTM) nuclear deals, and utility switchyard capacity hoarding that locks out competitors from regional grids.
lead_story.mechanism: Hyperscalers are executing 20-year exclusive take-or-pay bilateral contracts with nuclear operators (such as Susquehanna and PJM generator busbars). By monopolizing the few remaining gigawatt-scale generation interconnects before they reach public transmission lines, dominant cloud players effectively foreclose potential rival clusters from access to the physical grid.
lead_story.analogy: Imagine a rail baron buying not just the train tracks, but every coal mine and water tower along the mountain pass. Even if competing locomotive engines are free to enter the market, they cannot physically move an inch because one player bought out all the fuel at the source.
lead_story.pr_claim: We are investing private capital to catalyze clean energy infrastructure and decarbonize the American power grid.
lead_story.pr_reality: Hyperscalers aren't building clean energy out of benevolence; they are aggressively fencing off the only baseload power plants in North America so competing AI labs starve in a 7-year utility queue.
lead_story.bull_take: Capitalizing power contracts secures multi-decade uptime moats, insulating sovereign hyperscalers from volatile public utility peak pricing.
lead_story.bear_take: Federal regulators and FERC will classify private BTM nuclear diversion as essential-facility foreclosure, slapping stranded-asset tariffs and common-carrier mandates on private switchyards by mid-2027.
lead_story.cascades: State public utility commissions halt fast-track datacenter zoning; regional commercial power tariffs jump 14% as public ratepayers absorb legacy grid upkeep.
lead_story.why_it_matters: The AI competitive landscape is no longer determined by who writes the best code; it is determined by who controls physical megawatts at the busbar.
lead_story.cocktail_flex: Antitrust used to worry about software bundling; now the FTC is investigating whether tech giants are monopolizing the laws of thermodynamics.

deep_dive.headline: Capacity Foreclosure: The Thermodynamics and Antitrust Law of Exclusive Nuclear Busbar PPAs
deep_dive.thesis: When tech conglomerates contract 100% of a nuclear station's generator output Behind-the-Meter, they withdraw firm baseload capacity from the regional wholesale market. Under the antitrust Essential Facilities Doctrine and Clayton Act Section 7, regulatory agencies are preparing to treat electrical switchyard interties as critical economic bottlenecks subject to non-discriminatory access mandates.
deep_dive.physics_breakdown: In traditional grid operations, large thermal and nuclear plants provide critical rotational inertia through multi-ton spinning turbines, stabilizing system frequency at 60 Hz (or 50 Hz). When hyperscalers divert baseload busbars to direct DC rectifiers, the public grid loses both active power and essential dynamic reactive support, forcing utilities to fire expensive, carbon-heavy peaker plants to balance residential load swings.

matrix.mechanism: Direct generator busbar co-location isolating nuclear generation behind private 500kV step-down switchyards.
matrix.audit: Corporate greenwashing masks an aggressive capacity grab that shifts transmission upgrade costs onto local households while creating structural antitrust moats.
matrix.cascades: FERC mandates cost-allocation tariffs on BTM interconnects; state regulators condition datacenter permits on constructing dedicated replacement generation.

deep_dive.takeaway: The next frontier of antitrust law will not be fought over operating systems or app store fees; it will be litigated over access to high-voltage generator busbars and regional thermal inertia.
